owner_decisions: ML-KEM-1024 SE inner wrap DESCOPED 2026-07-07 (CLAUDE.md invariant #3, work-todo #9) — do not re-raise; a PQ-sealed *backup* artifact is a separate roadmap item (docs/feature-roadmap-research-2026-06.md:126) but must not be argued as the bus wrap.
SSD1306 OLED backend removed 2026-06-30; NV3007 LCD is the only shipping display (CLAUDE.md feature flags). Do not reintroduce OLED or propose OLED-specific mitigations.

Pixel trusted-UI pilot `ui-px` is an owner decision (2026-09-22) and scroll-to-end `PX_COMMIT_REQUIRES_SEEN_LAST = true` (2026-09-24) — 'do not re-litigate without new evidence'. Any seed-display change must keep the px path as the primary pq1 wizard path.

Atlas lives in the NS slot (owner decision 2026-09-23); the secret run therefore reads glyph bitmaps from NS flash by design — proposals must not move the atlas into the secure image on emanation grounds alone (the secure slot is already 76,949 B over budget with ui-px).

Consumption mask is production-mandatory (nsc/mod.rs ship-blocker fence) and its unloaded-pin status is an accepted 'satisfied-by-construction' caveat per CLAUDE.md; port of a Trezor GPDMA-driven mask is a listed follow-up, not a decision.

'No software PRNG' (CLAUDE.md What NOT to do) blocks a Trezor-style always-on RDI jitter (#805) until the owner resolves the PRNG-scope question; do not implement a DRBG-backed display jitter without that decision.

OPTIGA S-1/S-2/S-3 ship-blockers and the first-boot/RDP-2 ceremony are deferred by design (CLAUDE.md pre-production caveats); display-surface findings must not be framed as ship-blockers of that class.

Owner priority for #237/#258/#260 is 'priority:low' on the tracker; the remaining stage-E mitigations (low-brightness wizard mode, one-word-at-a-time reveal, constant-weight encoding, shielding) are listed as candidates with no decision recorded — the downstream agent should present them as options, not as agreed work.

Dual-SE XOR split is deliberately preferred over host-visible Shamir/SLIP-39 (docs/architecture/trezor-comparison.md:472); any no-seed-display backup proposal must preserve invariant #1 (never reassemble both halves outside the secure world) and the cross-chain address stability of invariant #6.
